title: Updates on American's operation following FAA's nationwide ground stop
summary: We have resumed operations following the FAA nationwide ground stop. While some operational delays will continue, our teams are working to get customers on their way as quickly and safely as possible.

# Updates on American's operation following FAA's nationwide ground stop


[(English) (opens in new window) PDF 79 KB](https://s202.q4cdn.com/986123435/files/doc_news/Update-on-FAAs-nationwide-ground-stop-2026.pdf)


*Updated Sunday, November 15, 2026, 11 p.m. CT*


American is prepared to operate a largely normal schedule Monday, Nov. 16, following the FAA's nationwide ground stop. With crews and aircraft in position and favorable weather expected across our system, we are set up for a good start to the week and do not anticipate additional broad cancellations related to this incredibly disruptive industry-wide event.


Our team continues to work around the clock to take care of our customers, and our[travel alert](https://www.aa.com/travelalerts) remains in effect, providing customers with options to change their plans or request a refund. Customers should continue to check their flight status on the American app or aa.com before heading to the airport.


We're grateful to all of our customers for their understanding and to our team members for everything they've done to support our recovery efforts.


---


*Updated Sunday, November 15, 2026, 12:55 p.m. CT*


American’s recovery from Friday’s FAA nationwide ground stop continues to move forward. We are seeing improvement today with fewer cancellations as we continue working to fully restore the operation.


We have extended our[travel alert](https://www.aa.com/travelalerts) to give customers greater flexibility with their plans, which they can use to change their reservation or request a refund. Customers traveling today should continue to check their flight status on the American app or aa.com before heading to the airport.


We appreciate our customers’ continued understanding and the tremendous work of team members across American as we continue our recovery.


---


*Updated Saturday, November 14, 2026, 8:55 p.m. CT*


American’s recovery from yesterday’s FAA nationwide ground stop continues to move forward. All planned cancellations for tonight and tomorrow have now been completed, though some individual flights may still be canceled as we continue working to fully restore the operation.


Our focus tonight is on setting up the operation for a strong start tomorrow, with our crews and aircraft positioned to get customers on their way. We continue to provide additional support for our crews reporting to work. We have also extended our[travel alert](https://www.aa.com/travelalerts) to give customers greater flexibility with their plans, which they can use to change their reservation or request a refund.


Customers traveling tonight or tomorrow should continue to check their flight status on the American app or aa.com before heading to the airport.


We appreciate our customers’ continued understanding and the tremendous work of our team members across American as we continue our recovery and prepare for tomorrow.


---


*Updated Saturday, November 14, 2026, 8:15 a.m. CT*


Yesterday's FAA nationwide ground stop led to significant cancellations and delays across our operation. Our team worked diligently through the night to restore our schedule and reposition aircraft and crews to protect today's operation.


While we are taking every step to limit the impact on our customers and team members, the lingering effects of this major disruption to the national airspace system will continue today, including additional delays and cancellations. We have taken a number of steps to support our recovery, including providing additional resources for crews reporting to work.


Customers traveling today should monitor their flight status on the American app or at[aa.com](https://www.aa.com/) before heading to the airport. For those with flexible travel plans, American has issued a[travel alert](https://www.aa.com/travelalerts) that allows customers to change their reservation or receive a refund.


To our customers: We're sorry for the impact FAA's nationwide ground stop has had on your travel plans. Our entire team is focused on getting you on your way. Thank you for the patience and grace you've shown our frontline team members as they do everything they can to assist you.


And to our team: Thank you for your incredible professionalism and resilience, and for the extraordinary care you continue to show our customers and each other.


---


*Updated Friday, November 13, 2026, 8:25 p.m. CT*


With the FAA’s five-hour nationwide ground stop lifted, American Airlines is focused on operating as many remaining flights as possible this evening while positioning the airline for the strongest possible recovery tomorrow and in the days ahead.


For the remainder of the evening, we are prioritizing flights to non-hub cities, as well as international flying, to position aircraft and crew where they are needed to help restore our operation. We expect residual delays and cancellations tonight and into tomorrow following the FAA’s nationwide ground stop.


We’re grateful to our team members for their continued work to care for our customers and minimize the impact of this disruption as much as possible.


Customers are encouraged to check the status of their flights on the American app or at aa.com before heading to the airport. To provide additional flexibility to customers who want to change their travel plans, American has issued a[travel alert](https://www.aa.com/travelalerts) , which includes an option to receive a refund.


---


*Updated Friday, November 13, 2026, 6:30 p.m. CT*


The FAA’s nationwide ground stop remains in place, though some flights from certain airports are beginning to receive clearance to depart. Most departures remain paused, and we expect continued disruption to our schedule, including unavoidable cancellations. Teams across American are working to safely get additional flights moving and customers on their way as conditions allow. To provide customers with additional flexibility, we have issued a travel alert at[aa.com/travelalerts](https://www.aa.com/travelalerts) that allows customers to change their travel plans free of charge. We thank our customers for their patience and our team members for the extra care they are taking during a challenging situation.


---


*Friday, November 13, 2026, 4:10 p.m. CT*


The FAA has temporarily paused departures nationwide. Flights already in the air can continue to their destinations. We expect disruption to our schedule for the rest of the day, depending on the length of the FAA’s nationwide ground stop.


It will be all hands on deck across American to get customers on their way as soon as possible when the FAA lifts this ground stop.
